image_transform: Whole views; aspect-preserving fit into common tiles, padding and identical labels. No flip or content crop.
cadence: All recorded frames retained; 10 control frames per playback second; display only.

notes.text: Bring the retained plug toward the slot center and reduce its apparent tilt with a small compensated rotation; descend cautiously.
Maintain the visible lateral centering, reduce forward tilt with translation compensation, and approach the slot slowly.
Continue squaring the connector over the fixed slot, compensating the hand rotation to keep the tip centered; preserve clearance during alignment.
Square the plug axis while compensating tip motion and approach the visible socket opening; retain the existing grip.
The plug is centered over the visible opening and nearly touching it. Begin a short, straight insertion while keeping the grasp and orientation fixed.
Continue a shallow straight insertion with the plug visually centered, retaining the grip and monitoring its contact with the slot.
Advance another shallow increment into the slot with the current visual centering and orientation; keep the connector grasped.
Continue a short, slow insertion while preserving the visible centering. The plug-slot contact is partly occluded, so limit further travel and reassess.
Maintain alignment and advance only 0.75 mm. The connector remains over the opening, but seating is visually ambiguous; preserve the grip and reassess.
Make a final shallow downward increment without lateral motion; the plug covers the opening, but seating is still occluded.
Pause at the current insertion depth and retain the connector. The opening is occluded, so assess stability before applying further downward travel.
The plug remains centered and retained. Advance one millimeter in small increments to test further seating without changing lateral alignment.
Continue a limited straight seating motion, keeping the plug centered and grasp unchanged. The socket occludes the tip, so completion remains uncertain.
The plug base has stopped moving visibly despite hand descent. Ease upward slightly while retaining the grasp to avoid pushing against a potentially misaligned rim.
Hold steady after relieving downward travel. The connector remains at the socket mouth; its hidden tip makes seating uncertain, so avoid further forceful motion.
Withdraw a few millimeters while keeping the grasp to expose the plug-slot relationship; the stationary plug base during descent leaves alignment uncertain.
The lifted plug remains retained and laterally centered. Make a small depth-axis correction away from the camera while approaching, since the earlier contact may have been on the socket rim.
Approach the socket at the corrected depth-axis position with a short straight descent; the plug remains retained with a small visible gap above the opening.
Close the remaining visible gap at the adjusted position using a shallow descent, keeping the connector centered and retained.
Advance a shallow insertion at the corrected depth-axis position. The plug covers the slot mouth; maintain the grip and assess the visible body rather than assuming tracking proves seating.
Try another limited straight insertion at the adjusted alignment. Monitor movement of the visible plug body; the tip is hidden by the socket rim.
The visible plug has not followed the recent descent convincingly. Retract vertically to expose the mouth and relieve possible rim contact before revising alignment.
With the tip now clear of the mouth, shift it two millimeters farther from the camera and approach gently; lateral centering appears close.
Approach the visible opening at the revised depth position in a two-millimeter descent, holding orientation and grip fixed to compare tip motion with hand motion.
The tip is immediately above the slot at the revised depth alignment. Descend 1.5 mm with the grasp and orientation unchanged, checking for entry rather than relying on hand tracking.
Apply a submillimeter centering correction and shallow seating motion at the revised depth alignment. Keep the plug grasped; its tip remains occluded by the socket.
The connector body has stopped following hand descent. Slightly reduce the opening target and lift clear to check retention before correcting angular alignment.
The lifted connector follows the hand and is centered laterally. Approach the opening again with the slightly smaller grip target, leaving angular and depth-axis alignment unchanged to check entry.
Close the small visible gap with a controlled 1.5 mm descent at the current alignment and tighter grasp, then inspect whether the connector follows into the opening.
Lift clear of possible rim contact and make a small pitch correction, compensating hand translation to keep the plug tip near the opening's depth position.
The lifted plug is retained with a visible gap above the slot. Approach at the corrected pitch with a short vertical descent, preserving lateral centering.
Try a shallow seating increment at the corrected pitch. Watch the upper connector body as the tip becomes occluded, maintaining the tighter grip.
The visible tip again stops above the opening. Lift clear and test a small depth correction toward the camera, opposite the earlier unsuccessful depth adjustments, while retaining the current pitch.
Approach at the revised depth and pitch, adding a submillimeter leftward correction to center the visible tip over the slot. Keep the connector grasped.
Lift slightly and shift two millimeters toward the camera to test the remaining depth-axis alignment; lateral centering looks close, but entry is not confirmed.
Lower through the visible gap at the latest depth correction, keeping pitch and lateral centering fixed. Check whether the connector enters or stops on the rim.
Try a shallow seating increment at the latest depth alignment. Keep the retained plug centered and monitor for entry; the tip is hidden by the socket.
Entry remains unconfirmed after depth adjustments. Withdraw and test the opposite pitch correction, compensating translation approximately to preserve tip alignment while clear of the rim.
Approach the visible slot with the revised pitch and a one-millimeter depth correction, keeping the retained plug laterally centered.
Close the visible gap at the revised pitch with a two-millimeter straight descent. Compare connector-body motion against the fixed slot before making any further alignment change.
The connector rests at the socket mouth after several shallow approaches. Relax the fingers without moving the hand to check whether it remains supported in the slot.
The released connector remains upright at the opening. Raise the open hand slightly to inspect whether it stays supported without finger contact.
The connector stands at the mouth but full seating is unconfirmed. Regrasp its upper body and lift slightly to expose the slot and reassess alignment.
The connector tipped and is not retained. Open the fingers and lower around its body for recovery rather than continuing insertion with an empty grasp.
The tipped connector lies between the open fingertips. Center slightly on its body and close progressively at the current height to recover retention without pressing onto the block.
Lift the recently closed grasp five millimeters to check whether the diagonal connector is retained before attempting to straighten it.
The diagonal connector followed the lift. Raise it clear while beginning a small roll to straighten its visible axis, compensating hand translation around the grasp region.
The connector is no longer retained after the roll. Open the fingers, return the hand upright, and lower around the tipped body for a deeper recovery grasp.
The connector lies flat, forward and slightly right of the fingers. Recenter the open grasp toward its body with a little vertical clearance before closing.
Lower the open fingers around the flat connector for deeper pad overlap, then close progressively. Retention must be checked with a small lift.
Lift the closed grasp ten millimeters to verify recovery of the flat connector and expose its orientation before attempting to straighten it.
The recovered connector is hanging at an angle near the fingertip edges. Close fully and lift slowly for clearance, checking retention before rotating.
The connector follows the closed grasp but lies across the fingers. Lift for clearance and begin a small pitch rotation about the grasp region to turn its end downward; monitor retention.
The connector remains at the closed fingertips with its free end diagonally down-right. Begin turning that end downward while compensating hand position to preserve clearance and inspect retention.
The recovered connector follows the grasp and points down-right. Rotate it further toward vertical above the socket, compensating translation to keep the grasp region clear of the block.
Continue rotating the recovered connector toward vertical while keeping its grasp region above the block; verify that it follows the fingers rather than slipping.
The retained plug is still leaning slightly right. Continue straightening it above the opening with a compensated roll, keeping the grasp region clear of the block.
The connector has separated from the fingers and rests on the block. Open and return the hand toward upright with upward clearance before attempting another grasp.
Return the open hand upright above the loose connector, moving the grasp center slightly left and away from the camera. Keep clearance while recovering alignment.
Lower the open, upright fingers around the flat connector, which is now centered in the gap. Keep lateral position fixed and inspect pad overlap before closing.
